title: Three Centers — Source Seat, Christic Door, Twin Vessel
purpose: Populate the three already-canonical centers C_F, O and C_S with project anchors, names, functions and comparative archetypes without collapsing distinct persons, traditions or texts into literal identity claims.
governing_rule: A center is a typed role-slot in the Potato geometry. Many names, symbols and figures may illuminate a center by function, but role correspondence is not identity, equivalence, reincarnation, historical proof or authority over a person.

rights_and_subjecthood.non_target_rule: No person, community, religion or named figure is represented as a target, enemy list, punishment object or instruction for action merely because it appears in this atlas.
rights_and_subjecthood.dignity_rule: Living and historical persons remain subjects with their own dignity and context; project placement does not reduce a person to a symbol.
rights_and_subjecthood.no_identity_collapse: Comparative occupants are linked by typed relations such as source, throne, threshold, mediator, twin, descent, rejection, seed, witness or return. They are not silently asserted to be the same being.
rights_and_subjecthood.living_person_boundary: Tim Dooley appears as the project's self-described/persona anchor. The atlas does not convert project mythology into an independent historical, scientific or doctrinal claim about a living person.
rights_and_subjecthood.tradition_boundary: Jewish, Christian, Mesopotamian and project-native meanings are stored separately. A later Christian interpretation does not overwrite Jewish textual context; a project comparison does not overwrite either.
rights_and_subjecthood.accusation_boundary: Placement carries no implication of guilt, danger, moral rank, pathology or membership in a hostile category.

geometry.upper_center: C_F — center of the upper/source field and upper Door tip
geometry.relational_center: O — midpoint inside the shared Door where Axis and Plane cross
geometry.lower_center: C_S — center of the lower/manifestation field and lower Door tip
geometry.whole: Potato of Life remains the semantic whole; none of the three figure anchors replaces the whole.

primary_anchor.label: Tim Dooley
primary_anchor.relation: The project's Tim/Father/Gardener/Axis cluster is placed here because this coordinate specializes in source-orientation, duration, holding, House and cultivation.
primary_anchor.boundary: This is an internal project placement, not a claim that Jewish or Christian divine names are aliases for Tim Dooley.

comparative_archetypes.label: Ancient of Days
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Daniel distinguishes the Ancient of Days from the figure approaching with the clouds; the distinction is useful to the three-center model.

comparative_archetypes.label: Divine names: YHWH / Adonai / Elohim / Ehyeh / El Elyon
comparative_archetypes.boundary: These are names/titles for God within Jewish tradition, not project aliases for Tim or any human person.

comparative_archetypes.label: Abraham / patriarchal fatherhood
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Human fatherhood/ancestry comparator, not divine-source identity.

comparative_archetypes.label: Eden planter / cultivator motif
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Functional gardening comparator; Scripture does not name a separate 'Gardener' person here.

primary_anchor.label: Jesus Christ
primary_anchor.relation: The overlap is the project's threshold/mediation coordinate. Christian texts supply Door, Way, Son of Man, Word/Logos, rejected-stone/cornerstone and heaven-earth access motifs around Jesus.
primary_anchor.boundary: Christian identification of Jesus as Christ is represented as Christian theology. Jewish messianic and scriptural readings retain their own meanings.

comparative_archetypes.label: Jacob at Bethel
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Jacob is not treated as Jesus; the scene is a structural access-comparator linking stone, vertical passage, House and Gate.

comparative_archetypes.label: Moses
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Mediator comparator, not identity with the Door.

comparative_archetypes.label: Melchizedek / priest-king
comparative_archetypes.tradition: Jewish / biblical with later Christian reception
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Later Christian Hebrews develops this differently; the atlas preserves the earlier textual role before comparison.

comparative_archetypes.label: Messiah / one like a son of man
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Jewish readings are diverse; Christian identification with Jesus is a later Christian reading, not assumed as the only Jewish meaning.

comparative_archetypes.label: Temple / veil / high-priest access
comparative_archetypes.tradition: Jewish cultic architecture; later Christian reinterpretation
comparative_archetypes.boundary: An access-system comparator rather than a person-equivalence.

primary_anchor.label: Thomas / Didymus
primary_anchor.kind: New Testament disciple + later Thomasine twin tradition + project Twin/Vessel anchor
primary_anchor.relation: The lower center specializes in embodiment, testing, wounds, descent, seed, rejection, witness and return. Thomas/Didymus provides the canonical Twin name and the project's strongest human-facing mirror/Vessel role.
primary_anchor.boundary: The canonical New Testament does not say Thomas was Jesus' biological twin. Later Syriac/apocryphal Thomas traditions develop that identification.

comparative_archetypes.label: Thomas / Didymus in John
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Twin is an etymological/name fact; the identity of the other twin is not stated in the canonical New Testament.

comparative_archetypes.label: Judas Thomas in later Syriac / Acts of Thomas tradition
Joseph
comparative_archetypes.boundary: A descent-to-service and rejection-to-fruit comparator, not identity with Thomas.

comparative_archetypes.label: David / rejected-to-king reversal
comparative_archetypes.boundary: A Targumic tradition reads the rejected stone in Davidic/son-of-Jesse terms; Christian texts later apply Psalm 118 to Jesus.

comparative_archetypes.label: Judah and Dan lion motifs
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Biblical lion imagery belongs to the tribes/texts themselves; 'Lion of the World' is project-native wording.

comparative_archetypes.label: Isaac / Akedah
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Judaism does not require a Christian death-resurrection reading of the Akedah.

comparative_archetypes.label: Jonah
comparative_archetypes.tradition: Jewish / biblical with later Christian typology
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Three-day Christ typology is specifically Christian reception.

comparative_archetypes.label: Tammuz / Dumuzi
comparative_archetypes.tradition: Mesopotamian religion; mentioned polemically in Ezekiel
comparative_archetypes.boundary: Tammuz is not a biblical hero and is not Thomas. Ezekiel depicts women mourning Tammuz at the north gate as part of a condemned cultic scene; any Thomas/Tammuz relation is project-comparative only.

comparative_archetypes.label: Suffering / rejected servant motif
comparative_archetypes.tradition: Isaianic text with diverse Jewish and Christian interpretations
comparative_archetypes.boundary: The identity of the servant is interpreted differently across Jewish and Christian traditions; the atlas does not force one identification.

corridors.label: Source → Door
corridors.rule: Source/orientation becomes relation, communication and passage without the Source and Door becoming the same role.
corridors.textual_mirror: Daniel 7 is useful precisely because the Ancient of Days and the approaching human-like figure remain distinct.

corridors.label: Door → Twin/Vessel
corridors.rule: A threshold becomes embodied, tested and witnessed. Thomas asks the Way, confronts wounds and becomes a particularly strong mirror/verification figure in John and later Thomasine tradition.

corridors.label: Return → Source
corridors.rule: Descent/rejection is only generative when it returns as nourishment, witness, repair, service, fruit or renewed seed rather than permanent victimhood.

placement_law: Put names on centers only when their function is declared.
Put symbols around centers as satellites when they recur across several occupants.
Use corridors for partial overlap; do not force a figure into a center when only one motif matches.
Keep project-native titles visibly distinct from scriptural/historical names.
A figure may illuminate more than one center, but the relation must be typed and scoped.
The center map is for interpretation and navigation, never for targeting, ranking or declaring authority over real people.
